analysis: Examined the two head_text excerpts of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 326-582 and 583-954). The patch is documentation-only. It updates the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and extends the GLM5Next reasoning-control table row near lines 1147-1155, which is outside the supplied units. Visible excerpts are unchanged context: prefix-cache capability and telemetry schemas, heartbeat, service_reservation_released, inference_error, attestation_response, models_replace and related messages. No source code, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing logic changed. The documented behavior is consistent with the canonical threat model. Cache scope remains coordinator-authored; the prefix-cache telemetry (slots[].prefix_cache) carries counters only, with no prompt text, token IDs or cache keys, so T-041 and its leak #2 mitigation are not affected. Telemetry is described as observational and not an admission or routing input. inference_error is sanitized by the coordinator, and attestation_response requires status_signature, which is consistent with TB-002 and TB-009. The documented reasoning-parameter handling (null unset, summary no-ops, other members refused) is not visible in the supplied units. It reflects input validation in provider-swift GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift, which was not supplied, so I cannot verify that the code matches the doc. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. I found no new attack surface, no invalidated threat assumptions and no threat-model gaps in the supplied evidence. Remaining integration question: whether the reasoning-member refusal logic in GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift matches the doc. That is outside this batch.
